event: Convergence India (co-located with Smart Future Cities India, Satcom India, Broadcast India Show, India Internet of Things Expo — the "Digital Week" cluster)
organizer: Exhibitions India Group (EIG), jointly organised with India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO); supported by IndiaAI Mission, Digital India and MeitY
method: Full client-side JS scrape of the official 'List of Participants' directory page (a paginated, filterable widget backed by structured per-exhibitor fields: name, country, sector/category, hall, stand). All 43 pages (1,021 exhibitors) were walked programmatically in a live browser session by driving the widget's own 'Next' pagination control and reading the rendered DOM after each page (no public API endpoint was found; the dataset renders fully client-side with no separate JSON/XHR call visible in network traffic). Extracted counts (1,021 total, 872 India, 149 non-India) were cross-verified twice independently from the same live session and are internally consistent with the site's own '1,021 exhibitors found of 1,021 total' counter.
caveats: EDITION-LABEL AMBIGUITY: the participants page and its underlying dataset were accessed while the site's top navigation/branding already showed the NEXT edition ('34th Convergence India Expo, 23-25 March 2027' logo/footer), i.e. registration for 2027 was open. However the exhibitor list itself is evidently the 33rd edition's (23-25 March 2026, the most recently COMPLETED edition as of the 2026-08-22 access date): its exhibitor count (1,021) and country roster (Russia/Moscow, Taiwan, New Zealand pavilions) match the 33rd edition's own organizer-published statistics and press coverage, and no 2027 exhibitor signage was distinguishable in the data. Exhibition sites commonly leave the prior edition's exhibitor directory live while opening next-year registration; treat this dataset as the 2026 (33rd) roster, carried over and not yet cleared for 2027 — the same caveat pattern the RailTrans Expo README flagged for a mismatched year label.

country_origin here is the exhibiting STAND's registered country per the organizer's own directory, not the ultimate parent company's global HQ. Several globally foreign-headquartered brands (Amazon Web Services / AWS, Google, Microsoft, Zoom, Telit Cinterion, Siemens) are listed with country_origin = India, because they exhibited via their Indian subsidiary/entity registration (e.g. 'Google India Pvt. Ltd.', 'Qualcomm India Pvt. Ltd.', 'Amazon Web services'). These are correctly excluded from the FOREIGN flag under this dataset's flag_basis (the site's own country field), but are worth a manual follow-up pass if the use case cares about ultimate parent HQ rather than exhibiting-entity registration.

Country string casing was inconsistent in the source (e.g. 'CHINA' vs 'China' for different rows) and was normalized to title case in country_origin; the raw as-scraped string is preserved verbatim inside each row's flag_basis quote.

A handful of rows have empty category_segment or hall/stand (e.g. trade associations, some 'Startup Odisha'-type state pavilions) — these are exhibitor-directory entries without an assigned physical booth (associations, government bodies) rather than parsing failures.

Some name pairs are near-duplicates referring to the same exhibitor under slightly different listing names or repeat stand numbers (e.g. 'Amazon Web services' and 'AWS'; 'Tait' and 'Tait Communications'; 'Diagnomitra Healthcare Solutions Private Limited' and 'diagnomitra healthcare solutions pvt ltd') — left as separate rows exactly as the source lists them, not de-duplicated, since the source itself treats them as separate directory entries (sometimes with different stand numbers).

'Country Pavilion' appears as a category_segment value (not a country) for a small number of umbrella/pavilion-organizer entries (Moscow Center Of International Cooperation, New Zealand Trade & Enterprise, Taiwan Excellence/TAITRA, Anpo Moscow Export Centre) — these are the pavilion organizers themselves, counted once each alongside the individual foreign companies exhibiting under their pavilions.
